name: Switzerland
sources: GDP $269.8bn and population 6.72m: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, series CHE, 1990 (269,768,238,555 and 6,715,519). CAVEAT, stated rather than hidden: Swiss nominal GDP in 1990 on the national accounts was about CHF 331bn, and converting that at the 1990 average market rate of 1.389 CHF/USD gives roughly $238bn, some 12% below the figure entered. The gap is the World Bank's Atlas-style conversion, not a disagreement about Swiss output. Consistency with the rest of the roster - which is all NY.GDP.MKTP.CD - is why the World Bank figure is the one in the file. Six and three-quarter million people with more output than Belgium and the Netherlands put together is not an artefact; the conversion method only moves the last digit or two.

Inflation 5.4%: World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG, CHE 1990 = 5.404%. Startlingly high for the country whose whole monetary reputation was low inflation, and the reason is domestic: a property and construction boom that the Swiss National Bank had been tightening against since 1988.

Policy rate 8.8%: three-month euro-Swiss-franc deposit rate, monthly mean of 1990 = 8.84% (OECD MEI via FRED, IR3TED01CHM156N). Higher than the Dutch or German rate in the same year, which for Switzerland is the whole story of 1990 in one number.

Revenue 24% of GDP: OECD Revenue Statistics, total tax revenue as a share of GDP, Switzerland 1990 (about 23.6%). The lowest in Western Europe by a distance and about half the Swedish figure - the federal government raises little and the cantons raise the rest, and direct democracy on tax rates keeps both down. NOTE: the World Bank's central-government revenue series shows Switzerland at 14.3% for 1990, and that number is not wrong, it is simply the Confederation alone with the cantons and communes left out. This field is general government, so the OECD figure is the correct one to enter.
Gross public debt 33% of GDP: IMF World Economic Outlook GGXWDG_NGDP, CHE 1990 = 32.8%. Below Germany's 0.41.
Military 1.6% of GDP: World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS (SIPRI), CHE 1990 = 1.572%.

Strength index 14: about 3,500 professional soldiers and a mobilisation strength near 625,000 reachable inside forty-eight hours, with some 380 Leopard 2 and Pz 68 tanks and a fortified Alpine redoubt built to be held after the plateau is lost. Indexed below Sweden's 18 - the same militia idea with a fraction of the defence industry and no navy - and below Spain's 16, and above Austria's 6, which is the other armed neutral in this region and a quarter the mobilised mass.

Gross fixed capital formation 32.7% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS, CHE 1990, the highest ratio in Western Europe that year and itself a symptom of the construction boom. Split into public 3.5% and private 29.2% using the AMECO general-government series, private as residual. CAVEAT: total transcribed, public share entered from reference knowledge of AMECO.

Stability 85 and authoritarianism 0.09: the highest stability on the board, above Germany's 80. The composition of the Federal Council had not changed since 1959 and no Swiss government has ever been removed by an election. Marked at 85 rather than higher for two things in the immediate record: the Fichenaffare broke in November 1989, when a parliamentary inquiry found the federal police had kept secret index cards on some 900,000 people, and on 27 November 1990 the Federal Supreme Court had to order Appenzell Innerrhoden to let women vote in cantonal affairs - nineteen years after the federal franchise. A state that placid with those two facts in it is an 85, not a 95.

Separatism 0.04: just below Italy's 0.05, and specific. The Jura question is a live territorial dispute inside the confederation - canton Jura was created out of Bern in 1979 after a referendum, the southern Jura districts voted to stay with Bern, and in 1989 the Laufen district voted to leave Bern for Basel-Landschaft. It is separatism that is settled by ballot on a schedule rather than by anything else, which is why the number is small and not zero.

TFP trend 0.008: below Spain's 0.009 and the lowest in this Western European batch, which looks perverse for the richest country in it and is not. Swiss real GDP was essentially flat from 1991 to 1997 - the worst growth performance in the OECD over that stretch - as the property boom unwound and a cartelised domestic sector faced no competition. A rich country that grows slowly is exactly what a productivity trend is for; entering a high number because the level is high would be modelling the wrong thing.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.6287%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series CHE (Switzerland): 6,441,865 in 1984 to 6,646,912 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 11 were held and are listed below with their citations; 37 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_packet_internetworking, core_single_mode_fiber, core_carbon_composites, core_combined_cycle_turbine, comp_risc_superscalar, comm_fibre_optic_backbone, comm_geostationary_comsat, ener_seismic_3d_imaging, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, matl_semiconductor_lithography, matl_composite_structures, matl_industrial_robotics, matl_lean_production, matl_single_crystal_superalloy, matl_rare_earth_magnet, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_pulse_doppler_radar, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_quiet_submarine, aero_recon_satellite, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_automated_sequencing, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, tran_electronic_freight_documents, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_protected_cultivation, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_marine_aquaculture, agri_flue_gas_desulphurisation.

SECOND AUTHORING PASS, 2026-08-31, USE-SIDE ONLY. The first pass was correctly instructed to rule NOT HELD when unsure, and produced a defensible but ragged board: the convergence channel was reading that transcription's INCOMPLETENESS as this nation's IGNORANCE, and paying it to catch up to things it already had. A second pass therefore re-ruled the 31 USE-SIDE nodes against an explicit standard published before any nation was looked at, each limb written separately into every source string. LIMB A: a citable fact putting the technology in general commercial or public service across the OECD on or before 31 December 1989, asserted once per technology and identical for every nation. LIMB B: the nation is in the Advanced Set - 1990 OECD member AND World Bank high-income in the 1990 groupings AND one of the 29 authored majors: australia canada france germany italy japan netherlands spain sweden switzerland uk usa. LIMB C: a performed and RECORDED search for a named fact placing the nation outside that deployment; a silent limb C is a failed limb C. Where limb A failed for a technology the board said so and fell back to the first pass's named-artefact bar rather than granting on the class claim - which is why several second-pass refusals contradict the brief's own opening cut. THE SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE BAR IS UNCHANGED: producing a jet engine is still producing a jet engine, and not one of the 17 sovereignty-side ids was added, removed or re-reasoned by this pass. THE PASS IS ADDITIONS-ONLY - no first-pass grant was removed or weakened - and it was authored blind of model output, with the simulation never run and no CAGR, gap or instrument reading consulted. ADDED BY THE SECOND PASS FOR THIS NATION, 3 cells: bio_cross_sectional_imaging (health and agriculture board), bio_monoclonal_antibody (health and agriculture board), core_pcr (health and agriculture board). The refused list above has been reduced by exactly those ids and by nothing else; every other first-pass refusal stands untouched, and each new grant carries its own citation below.

granted.source: Route (b), inherited from comp_microprocessor: World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 9.02 PCs per 100. (Switzerland is the nation the review used as its falsifier - richest per head, and the derived model gave it 38 technologies. It gets four of my six, and none of the two sovereignty-side ones.)

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E2: Pauli U, Beutler B, Peterhans E, 'Porcine tumor necrosis factor alpha: cloning with the polymerase chain reaction and determination of the nucleotide sequence', Gene 1989;81(1):185-91 (PMID 2478420), Institute for Veterinary Virology, University of Berne. Corroborated by 'A simple method for direct cloning and sequencing cDNA by the use of a single specific oligonucleotide and oligo(dT) in a polymerase chain reaction', Nucleic Acids Research 1989 (PMID 2911482), Institute of Pharmacology and Biochemistry, University Zurich-Irchel - a METHOD-IMPROVEMENT paper, which means the Zurich group was refining PCR in 1989, not acquiring it. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found.
World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 9.02 PCs per 100, 3.7x the World value of 2.45.
Oracle established a Swiss subsidiary within three years of 1982 (Oracle corporate histories, as above). Switzerland also holds comp_microprocessor at 9.02 PCs per 100.

R3: the Swiss NMT-900 network (Natel C) opened in September 1987 (Nordic Mobile Telephone country launch record). World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 125,047 Swiss mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.

Project Megawatt - Markus Real's Alpha Real programme in Zurich, which from 1987 installed 333 grid-connected 3 kW crystalline-silicon rooftop arrays, roughly a megawatt in total, and is the first programme anywhere to treat grid-connected rooftop photovoltaics as a deployable product rather than an experiment. The 100 kW plant on the A13 motorway noise barrier near Domat/Ems, 1989, was the first photovoltaic installation on a motorway sound wall. Switzerland is a small board cell that earns its place: for grid-connected crystalline photovoltaics it was ahead of every country here except the United States.

Roferon-A, recombinant interferon alfa-2a, was manufactured by F. Hoffmann-La Roche at Basel and approved by the FDA in June 1986 for hairy cell leukaemia — one of the first two recombinant interferons licensed anywhere. Switzerland was therefore producing a recombinant protein drug on its own soil, for its own and export markets, four years before the start date. FLAGGED: the hard date I hold is an American approval of a Swiss-made product; a Swissmedic-predecessor (IKS) registration date would make this cell airtight.
WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 coverage, Switzerland, 1990: 90%. Series: WUENIC DTP3 ('Switzerland,CHE,1990,90').

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E2, two dated 1989 Swiss clinical series, one per modality, at two different universities. (i) CT: Ettlin TM, Staehelin HB, Kischka U, Ulrich J et al., 'Computed tomography, electroencephalography, and clinical features in the differential diagnosis of senile dementia. A prospective clinicopathologic study', Archives of Neurology 1989;46(11):1217-20 (PMID 2818257), Neurological Clinic, University of Basel. (ii) MRI: Mueller F, Haenny P, Wichmann W, Fierz W et al., 'Cerebrospinal fluid immunoglobulins and multiple sclerosis. Correspondence with magnetic resonance imaging and visually evoked potential changes', Archives of Neurology 1989;46(4):367-71 (PMID 2468328), Department of Neurology, University Hospital, Zurich. Both are prospective clinical series in which the imaging is the routine investigation rather than the object of study, which is what distinguishes service from demonstration under section 1.3. LIMB C SEARCHED: no citable fact places Switzerland outside the deployment; I found no Swiss moratorium, cantonal bar or published shortfall. Grant rests on the MRI-and-conventional-CT half.

NAMED-ARTEFACT BAR, CLASS E2, and the earliest non-American cell in this technology: Widmer U, Frei D, Keusch G, Burger HR et al., 'OKT3 treatment of steroid- and/or anti-thymocyte globulin-resistant renal allograft rejection occurring on triple baseline immunosuppression including cyclosporine A', Transplantation Proceedings 1988;20(5 Suppl 6):90-5 (PMID 3140454), Department of Internal Medicine, University Hospital, Zurich, October 1988. Six pages on OKT3 as third-line rescue within a defined triple-immunosuppression protocol is service, not first use. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found.
